newsitem.title: GERMANY: Deutsche -no need to respond to new merger.
newsitem.headline: Deutsche -no need to respond to new merger.

text.p: Deutsche Bank AG said on Wednesday is saw no need to take any action in response to the planned merger of Bayerische Vereinsbank AG with Bayerische Hypotheken- und Wechsel-Bank AG.
Deutsche also said that it no longer regarded its 5.21 percent stake in Vereinsbank stake as a strategic stake.
Following news of the merger, the stake had become a pure financial investment which would be managed accordingly, Deutsche chief executive Rolf Breuer told a news conference.

"There is no need at all for Deutsche Bank to take action as a competitor," Breuer said, adding that Deutsche could flatter itself as having initiated or at least speeded up the process of banking mergers by announcing in July 1996 that it had bought a stake in Vereinsbank.

Breuer said that while the emergence of the new Bavarian bank, to be called Bayerische Hypo- und Vereinsbank AG, would create Germany's second largest bank and Europe's largest property financer, it did not mark a major change in the competitive environment outside Germany.

"The banking world in Bavaria and Germany has changed," Breuer said. But he added: "Our strategy is clearly different, we want to be a globally active investment bank and a focused universal bank. These aims have only been affected peripherally by the formation of a new number two in Germany."
He added that Deutsche took the new bank very seriously but said: "We are a different bank."
